newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks trade tightly, end up on thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks trade tightly, end up on thin turnover.

text.p: Greek stocks closed 0.26 percent higher after trading narrowly for most of the session on thin turnover and brokers said the farmers' blockade of roads and rails was taking centre stage in the oversold market.

"It was another day of low turnover with the market paying attention to the farmers' blockade," said Yannis Kalogerakis, head of trading at ABN-AMRO Axias Securities. "Valuations are attractive and earning yields compare favourably with the benchmark 12-month T-bill yield of 11.50 percent."
Farmers continued a 13-day blockade of major highways and road links protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget and vowing to spend the Christmas holidays by the roadblocks.
They were demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of the debts by farm cooperatives to state banks and higher price supports especially for cotton.
Talks between the socialist government and representatives of the farmers broke down on Wednesday leading to a deadlock.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis was chairing a cabinet meeting today trying to find a way to deal with the farmers' blockade and discuss matters relating to the 1997 pay of civil servants.
On Monday, national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou said the government would not bow to the farmers blackmail and would stick to its economic policies.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.26 percent or 2.30 points higher at 903.30 from Monday's 901.00 close after opening at 901.13. Turnover rose to 3.26 billion drachmas on volume of 2.5 million shares.
There were a couple of block trades with 37,000 shares of Papastratos trading at 4,575 drachmas and 508,000 shares of Hellenic Biscuits at 990 drachmas.

Losers led gainers 115 to 70 with 26 issues unchanged on 211 traded. Banks rose 0.05 percent, industrials gained 0.21 percent with construction also firmed 0.54 percent. Small-caps lost 0.34 percent. The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 550-568. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended up 55 drachmas at 4,245.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $7.01-$8.01. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 2,529-2,698 drachmas at the close. --Dimitrs Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
